q: In Microsoft Excel, what is a cell?
options: The file that holds many sheets
The intersection of a row and a column
A grid of rows and columns
explain: A cell is where a row and a column meet and is the basic data-entry unit. The file is a workbook and the grid is a worksheet.

q: Which program is widely recognised as the first personal-computer spreadsheet?
explain: VisiCalc is widely recognised as the first PC spreadsheet. Lotus 1-2-3 was a prominent DOS-based spreadsheet that came later.

q: Excel was first released for the Macintosh in 1985. In which year did the Windows edition follow?
explain: The Windows edition of Excel followed in 1987, two years after the Macintosh release.

q: Which cell address lies in row 13 and the 19th column?
explain: The 19th column is S, and in A1 notation the column comes before the row, so the address is S13.

q: What does the Name Box in Excel show?
options: The contents or formula of the active cell
The active cell address or a defined name
The name of the active sheet
explain: The Name Box shows the address (such as C7) or a defined name. The Formula Bar shows the contents or formula.

q: Which shortcut expands or collapses the Ribbon in Excel?
explain: Ctrl + F1 toggles the Ribbon. Ctrl + F4 closes the selected workbook window.

q: Which Excel tab holds functions, calculation options and formula tools?
explain: The Formulas tab is for functions, calculation and formula tools. The Data tab is for importing, sorting, filtering and managing data.

q: Which file extension identifies a macro-enabled Excel workbook?
explain: .xlsm is the macro-enabled workbook. .xltm is a macro-enabled template, and .xlsx cannot retain VBA code.

q: How many sheets does a new blank workbook normally contain in Excel 2016?
explain: Excel 2013 and later normally start with 1 sheet. Excel 2003, 2007 and 2010 started with 3.

q: What is the last column of an Excel 2007 (and later) worksheet?
explain: Modern worksheets have 16,384 columns, ending at XFD. The older Excel 2003 limit of 256 columns ended at IV.

q: What is the maximum number of characters a single Excel cell can hold?
explain: A cell can hold 32,767 characters. 255 is the maximum column width, not the text limit.

q: How many rows did a worksheet in Excel 2003 (.xls) have?
explain: Excel 2003 offered 65,536 rows x 256 columns. The 1,048,576 rows belong to Excel 2007 onward.

q: What are sparklines in Excel?
explain: Sparklines are tiny charts placed in single cells, in Line, Column or Win/Loss form. They are added from Insert > Sparklines.

q: Which function key opens the Save As dialog in Excel?
explain: F12 opens Save As. F2 edits the active cell and F11 creates a chart sheet.

q: Which shortcut starts a new line inside the same cell?
explain: Alt + Enter inserts a line break within the cell. Ctrl + Tab switches to the next open workbook window.

q: What does pressing F11 create in Excel?
options: A bar chart beside the data
A chart sheet with the default chart type
explain: F11 makes a chart on a separate chart sheet using the default chart type - not specifically a bar chart. Shift + F11 inserts a worksheet.

q: Which shortcut inserts AutoSum in Excel?
explain: Alt + = inserts AutoSum (check the proposed range). Shift + F3 opens Insert Function and Alt + F11 opens the VBA editor.

q: Which shortcut selects an entire column?
explain: Ctrl + Spacebar selects the column, while Shift + Spacebar selects the row. Ctrl + 9 hides rows.

q: What does the shortcut Ctrl + ; do in Excel?
options: Inserts the current date as a fixed value
Inserts the current date and time together
Applies a date format to the selection
explain: Ctrl + ; types today's date as a fixed value that does not update. Ctrl + Shift + 3 only applies a date format.

q: Which of these entries updates automatically whenever Excel recalculates?
explain: Functions such as =NOW() and =TODAY() are recalculated, whereas shortcut entries and typed dates stay fixed.

q: What does ##### in a cell usually indicate?
options: The column is too narrow for the formatted value
explain: Hashes usually mean the column is too narrow for a formatted number or date. Widening or AutoFitting the column fixes it, and no data is lost.

q: With cell B2 selected, Freeze Panes keeps which parts visible while scrolling?
explain: Freeze Panes freezes everything above and to the left of the selected cell, so row 1 and column A stay visible.

q: When cells that all contain data are merged in a left-to-right sheet, what content is retained?
explain: Merging keeps only the upper-left content and discards the rest after confirmation. It does not concatenate the text.

q: What does the formula =MOD(17,5) return?
explain: MOD returns the remainder: 17 = 5 x 3 + 2, so the result is 2.

q: When a workbook is exported as CSV, what is normally saved?
options: The active sheet's displayed text and values
The charts and formulas of every sheet
Only the formulas of the active sheet
explain: CSV export saves the active sheet's displayed values as plain text; formatting, charts and extra sheets are not preserved.

q: A red triangle in a cell's upper-right corner in modern Excel indicates a...
explain: In modern Excel the red triangle marks a Note (the traditional comment). Modern Comments support threaded discussions.

q: The reference A1 is copied two columns to the right and two rows down. What does it become?
explain: A relative reference shifts with the copy: column A moves to C and row 1 moves to row 3.

q: Which of the following is a mixed cell reference?
explain: A$9 fixes only the row (9), so it is mixed. $A$9 and $A$5 are absolute; A9 is relative.

q: How many cells are there in the range A10:D30?
explain: The range has 4 columns and 30 - 10 + 1 = 21 rows, so 4 x 21 = 84 cells.

q: What does Goal Seek do in Excel?
options: Saves and compares sets of inputs
Calculates results for several inputs in a table
Counts the cells that meet a condition
Finds the input needed for a target formula result
explain: Goal Seek adjusts one input cell to reach a chosen result. Scenario Manager compares input sets and a Data Table shows results for varying inputs.

q: Cells A1 to A5 hold: Qty (text), 50, an empty cell, 5.5 and 10. What does =COUNTA(A1:A5) return?
explain: COUNTA counts every non-empty cell: Qty, 50, 5.5 and 10 make 4. COUNT would give 3 and COUNTBLANK would give 1.

q: What does =COUNT(1,"a","b") return?
explain: COUNT counts only numeric arguments, so just the number 1 is counted; the text values "a" and "b" are ignored.

q: In =VLOOKUP(E2,A2:C20,3,FALSE), what does the FALSE argument request?
options: A search in the last column
explain: FALSE requests an exact match. The 3 selects the table's third column as the value to return.

q: Column A (rows 2 to 10) lists Pen, Pencil, Binder, Pen, Gel Pen, Binder, Pencil, Binder, Pen, and row 1 is a heading. What does =COUNTIF(A1:A10,"*Pen*") return?
explain: The wildcard matches Pen (3 times), Pencil (2 times) and Gel Pen (once), giving 6. COUNTIF counts matching cells, not quantities.

q: Which wildcard character matches exactly one character in functions such as COUNTIF?
explain: The question mark matches a single character, so P?n matches Pen but not Pencil. The asterisk matches any sequence, and ~ escapes a wildcard.

q: What does =SUM(8/4/2,1-2/2) return?
explain: Divisions run left to right: 8/4/2 = 1 and 1-2/2 = 0, so SUM(1,0) = 1.

q: What does =SUM(5,5,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE) return?
explain: Logical values typed directly as arguments count as TRUE = 1 and FALSE = 0, so 5+5+1+0+1+0 = 12.

q: What does =CEILING(19,4)+FLOOR(19,4) return?
explain: CEILING(19,4) is 20 (next multiple of 4 at or above) and FLOOR(19,4) is 16 (at or below), so the total is 36.

q: What does =FACT(0)+FACT(3)+FACT(5) return?
explain: 0! is defined as 1, 3! = 6 and 5! = 120, so the sum is 1 + 6 + 120 = 127.

q: Which chart type is best for showing one data series as parts of a whole?
explain: A pie chart shows a single series as shares of a total. Line charts show trends and column charts compare categories.
